done_when: Every status, count and time on the board page and in forge board --json comes from one shared derivation, so they agree: stories the roadmap marks done count and show as done; items idle past the stalled threshold show as stalled with their idle time and what they wait on, and finished items never do; a running worker or review shows as running with its elapsed time; ready-to-merge, plan-read and waiting-for-approval stages match forge next; a finished story's parts show finished; prose and timeline times agree; header counts are labelled separately for stories and fixes; a person shows under one display name; titles are shortened at a word boundary; command tests reproduce each of these on a board with real-shaped data for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: Raise: Gate — The new test file deterministically fails the repository’s required test-naming check. Both functions at lines 125 and 143 claim criterion 3 under STORY="FIX-BOARD-DATA-TRUTH"; functions at lines 193 and 226 likewise duplicate criterion 4. tests/test_rules.py:47–50 rejects duplicate (story, criterion) pairs. The full suite configured in forge.toml includes that check; the supplied 69-case related run does not. Give both pairs distinct criterion numbers while retaining their assertions.
findings.title: Not done: required tests check

findings.body: Raise: Not done — The previously reported completion-date defect remains open: a story marked done by the roadmap, with historical state but no recorded completion timestamp, displays its creation date as “Finished on”. This fallback accepts history["dates"] for stories, but src/forge/board.py:720–727 populates those dates from the state file’s first addition, potentially weeks before completion. Both JSON and the current card therefore report an invented completion date. The named roadmap-only proof has neither historical state nor a Git creation date, so it misses this case. Preserve unknown completion dates for stories without completion evidence; retain the first-addition fallback for tasks and fixes.
findings.title: Not done: Every status, count and time on the board page and in forge board --json comes from one shared derivation

findings.body: Raise: Test — The proof list claims this test protects the one-day stalled threshold, but its only unfinished idle item has been idle for four days. Changing the threshold from one day to three days would leave this test and the other supplied idle assertions green, while ordinary items idle for 25 hours would incorrectly remain unstalled. Add a command-level assertion just beyond the promised one-day threshold to the existing test, covering both client histories.

why: The forge board page shows wrong or contradicting data (Opus review of a real client board, 2026-10-09): stories the roadmap marks done show as 'Not started yet' and count as needing a spec; items idle for days aren't shown as stalled while finished stories are flagged stalled; running workers and reviews show as 'Needs fixes'; a card says Ready to merge while the header counts none; a story in a plan-read round shows as 'Waiting for approval'; a finished story's part says 'In progress'; prose times disagree with the timeline; header counts mix stories and fixes unlabelled; one person appears under two names; fix titles are cut mid-word
